BorelRegulators.summary: Almost nothing in the Borel-regulator chain exists. Neither library has algebraic K-theory above K₀, so the rank theorem, the regulators r_j and their covolumes have no carrier; arithmetic-group infrastructure exists only in SL₂(ℤ)/SL_n(ℤ) special cases — Mathlib's SL₂(ℤ) = ⟨S, T⟩ and Schreier's lemma, Tau Ceti's SL_n(ℤ) generation by transvections, and the SL₂(ℤ) fundamental domain with finite volume (Mathlib ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd, Tau Ceti ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top) — while Weil restriction of group schemes, Siegel sets, Borel–Serre, Tamagawa measures and orders in division algebras are absent (general Haar measure, the adele ring and central simple algebras exist). Continuous group cohomology exists (Mathlib's homogeneous cochain complex, with Tau Ceti's restriction/inflation and a low-degree explicit model), but relative Lie-algebra cohomology, invariant forms on G/K and van Est do not. Towards R.4–R.5 the libraries have only the j = 1 shadow — NumberField.Units.regulator as the covolume of the full unit lattice, and the Dedekind zeta function with its residue formula (Mathlib) and Euler product (Tau Ceti) — and lack the continuation and functional equation of ζ_F, any order-of-vanishing statement, Deligne cohomology, the Bloch–Wigner function (Mathlib has only Li_s on the unit circle, HurwitzZeta.expZeta) and every Tamagawa-measure statement.

targets.target: Restriction of scalars (Weil restriction) for algebraic groups, and the induced arithmetic subgroup
targets.note: Neither library has Weil restriction of scalars for group schemes or algebraic groups: greps for `weilRestriction`, `WeilRestriction`, `RestrictionOfScalars` over group objects return nothing. Only module/algebra-level restriction of scalars (Mathlib's `RestrictScalars`, Tau Ceti's `CommAlgCat.restrictScalars`) exists, which is the wrong direction.

targets.target: Haar measure and Tamagawa measure on an adelic algebraic group
targets.note: General Haar measure on a locally compact group and the adele ring of a number field both exist, but nothing named or described as a Tamagawa measure does: `grep -rn -i tamagawa` over both trees returns no hits. The convergence factors, local measures and their product are absent.

targets.target: Reduction theory: minimal rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite covering of the arithmetic quotient, finite volume
targets.note: Only the classical SL₂(ℤ) case exists. Mathlib proves every point of ℍ is SL₂(ℤ)-equivalent to a point of the standard fundamental domain 𝒟 (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd); Tau Ceti proves 𝒟 has finite invariant volume (ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top), that its interior is a measure-theoretic fundamental domain for PSL₂(ℤ) (isFundamentalDomain_fdo), and tiles a fundamental domain for every subgroup by cosets. Minimal rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite covering and finite volume for a general arithmetic group — AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.3's targets — are absent; the value vol(SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ) = π/3 is not proved either.

targets.target: Borel–Serre compactification, finite-complex models for arithmetic quotients, torsion-stabilizer descent
targets.note: `borel.serre` matches nothing in either library; there is no manifold-with-corners compactification of a locally symmetric space and no finiteness-property theory for arithmetic groups.

targets.target: Orders in central division algebras over a number field, and Borel's block-inclusion maps
targets.note: Central simple algebras, Wedderburn, Skolem–Noether, splitting and the Brauer group are developed in both libraries (Mathlib.Algebra.Central/BrauerGroup, TauCeti.Algebra.CentralSimple/BrauerGroup), but the *arithmetic* of orders — maximal orders in a division algebra over a number field, their unit groups as arithmetic groups — is absent (`maximal order` matches nothing).

targets.target: Finite generation / finite-type homotopy properties of arithmetic groups
targets.note: Finite generation is available for the simplest arithmetic groups only. Mathlib proves SL₂(ℤ) = ⟨S, T⟩ (SpecialLinearGroup.SL2Z_generators), Schreier's lemma that finite-index subgroups of finitely generated groups are finitely generated (instance Subgroup.fg_of_index_ne_zero), finite index of the congruence subgroups Γ(N), Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N), and finite generation of (𝓞_K)ˣ (a Monoid.FG instance in Units/DirichletTheorem.lean); Tau Ceti proves SL_n(ℤ) is generated by elementary transvections. Group.FG for SL₂(ℤ) or its congruence subgroups is not stated, and there is no finite-generation or finite-presentation theorem for general arithmetic groups (Borel–Harish-Chandra), no finite-type classifying space and no finite-type homotopy result.

duplicates.note: AA.3 is the declared owner of Siegel sets, reduction theory, finite covering and finite volume; R.1 restates the same targets as an import and then specialises them to division-algebra orders.
ALS.2 owns the Borel–Serre compactification, its manifold-with-corners structure and the homotopy equivalence from the interior, which R.1 lists as imported targets.

N.3:finite-generation proves finite generation of K_n(O_{F,S}) and explicitly develops 'the arithmetic-group finiteness and finite-type homotopy input in Quillen's proof', the same finiteness infrastructure R.1 asks for.
AA.1 constructs the base-change and restriction-of-scalars equivalences for adelic points, the restriction of scalars R.1 lists first among its imported targets.
AA.2 constructs Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms and convergence factors, the Haar/Tamagawa-measure target R.1 imports.

targets.target: Continuous group-cochain complex of a topological group with topological coefficients
targets.note: Mathlib defines the homogeneous continuous cochain complex TopRep.homogeneousCochains and continuousCohomology for any topological group acting on a topological module (action continuous on the module only), built from iterated C(G, C(G, …)) rather than C(Gⁿ, M); its TODO lists the n-ary description, the comparison with group cohomology and long exact sequences as missing. Tau Ceti adds restriction and inflation in all degrees on this object, and a separate explicit inhomogeneous model (TauCeti.ContCohomology) in degrees ≤ 2 with a long exact sequence, Shapiro (degrees 0–1), corestriction (0–2) and low-degree cup products. This covers the continuous-cochain complex; it is not specialised to real Lie groups, and there is no differentiable-cochain complex or smoothing comparison.

targets.target: Relative Lie-algebra cochain complex C*(g,K;V) and its cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib has only the bottom of the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex — one- and two-cochains with d₁₂, d₂₃ and two-cocycles, built for Lie-algebra extensions (file is sorry-free). There is no cochain complex in all degrees, no Lie-algebra cohomology functor, and nothing relative to a compact subgroup K.

targets.target: Complex of G-invariant V-valued differential forms on G/K and its identification with relative Lie cochains
targets.note: No invariant-form complex on a homogeneous space; `invariant forms` and `G/K` searches find only Lie-theoretic invariant bilinear forms (Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.InvariantForm), which is unrelated.

targets.target: van Est isomorphism H*_cont(G,V) ≅ H*(g,K;V)
targets.note: `vanest` matches no declaration and `van Est` no docstring in either tree.

targets.target: Comparison to the arithmetic subgroup; compatibility with block inclusions, primitive classes and coefficient extension
targets.note: Depends on the previous three targets and on arithmetic quotients, none of which exist.

duplicates.note: AF.1a is explicitly the owner of continuous/differentiable cochain complexes, the invariant-form complex on G/K, its identification with relative Lie cochains and van Est; R.2's first sentence imports exactly that list, leaving only the arithmetic-subgroup comparison as R.2's own content.

The full ALS.5 compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology of the arithmetic quotients in characteristic zero via local systems, using AF.1a; this is the arithmetic-subgroup comparison R.2 says it will construct.

targets.target: Stable cohomology of the compact duals of the classical groups (exterior algebra on primitive generators)
targets.note: Neither library computes H*(U(n);ℚ), H*(O(n);ℚ) or their stable limits; there is no cohomology ring of a Lie group at all, and no fibration-based computation.

targets.target: Stable-range comparison between arithmetic-group cohomology and the compact dual, with explicit bounds
targets.note: Requires the arithmetic quotients of R.1 and the invariant-form complex of R.2; none present.

targets.target: Rational Hurewicz theorem
targets.note: `hurewicz` matches no declaration in either library; Mathlib has no Hurewicz theorem, rational or integral.

targets.target: Plus-construction comparison K_n(R) = π_n(BGL(R)⁺)
targets.note: No plus construction: `plusConstruction`, `quillenPlus`, `BGL` all return nothing. There is no higher algebraic K-theory in either library.

targets.target: Borel's Proposition 12.2: rank K_i of an order in a central division algebra, period-four pattern 0, r₁+r₂, 0, r₂
targets.note: Only the invariants r₁, r₂ and the unit rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 of Dirichlet's theorem exist (K₁(O_F) ≅ O_F^× by Bass–Milnor–Serre, which neither library has; the class group belongs to K₀, not K₁). The theorem itself has no statement, since K_i is undefined for i ≥ 2.

duplicates.note: N.3:ranks states the same period-four rank formula for K_n(O_{F,S}); it declares that it consumes R.3's cohomology theorem rather than reproving it, so the two layers state the same conclusion at different generality (order in a division algebra vs S-integers).
K.2:plus owns the plus construction and the comparison π_n(BGL(R)⁺) ≅ K_n(R) that R.3 lists as an input.

targets.target: Normalised continuous-cohomology Borel classes and their pairing with K-theory homology classes
targets.note: `borelRegulator`, `borelClass` match nothing. Continuous cohomology exists as a functor (Mathlib ContinuousCohomology) but no specific classes for GL_n(ℂ) are constructed.

targets.target: The component regulator for an embedding F ↪ ℂ and complex-conjugation parity
targets.note: No construction. The regulators in the libraries are Mathlib's unit regulator NumberField.Units.regulator (and regOfFamily) and Tau Ceti's Néron–Tate regulator of an elliptic curve, WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator; there is no Borel regulator or any map on higher K-groups.

targets.target: The assembled map r_j : K_{2j-1}(F) → V_j(F) with dim V_j = r₁+r₂ (j odd), r₂ (j even), and its naturality/transfer/Adams-weight compatibilities
targets.note: K_{2j-1}(F) does not exist, so neither the source nor the map can be stated; Adams operations on K-theory are also absent.

targets.target: Determinant line, regulator covolume of the torsion-free K-group, and full-lattice image
targets.note: The j=1 instance of this exact package is fully proved in Mathlib: the unit lattice is a full ℤ-lattice (Dirichlet), its covolume is `NumberField.Units.regulator`, and `ZLattice.covolume` is the general covolume machinery with basis-independence. The roadmap document does not mention this. For j≥2 nothing exists.

targets.target: The Dedekind zeta function of a number field
targets.note: ζ_F is defined in Mathlib as the L-series of the ideal-counting function, and Tau Ceti proves its Euler product, non-vanishing for Re s > 1 and abscissa of absolute convergence. Both are sorry-free.

targets.target: Completed zeta with archimedean factors, analytic continuation and functional equation
targets.note: Mathlib has completion, continuation and the functional equation only for the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ (via Hurwitz zeta and Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.AbstractFuncEq), together with Deligne's Γℝ/Γℂ factors. Nothing continues ζ_F past Re s > 1 for a general number field, and there is no Hecke/Tate proof; `NumberField.dedekindZeta` has no continuation lemma.

targets.target: Tate integrals / Poisson summation route with normalised Haar measures and discriminant
targets.note: Poisson summation over ℝ and the adele ring exist, but there are no adelic Schwartz–Bruhat functions, no local or global Tate zeta integrals, and no adelic Poisson summation.

targets.target: Order of vanishing of ζ_F at 1−j equals dim V_j(F), for j≥2, and the leading coefficient
targets.note: Not statable: ζ_F is only defined on its half-plane of convergence, and V_j(F) is undefined. For F = ℚ Mathlib proves only vanishing and values at negative integers — ζ(−2n) = 0 (riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one), ζ(−n) via Bernoulli numbers, and the trivial zeros of even and odd Dirichlet L-functions — with no order-of-vanishing statement (no analyticOrderAt/meromorphicOrderAt result for any zeta or L-function) and no leading coefficient.

targets.target: Borel's regulator theorem: rational proportionality of the leading coefficient and the regulator covolume
targets.note: The j=1 analogue — the Dirichlet class number formula relating the residue of ζ_F at s=1 to the regulator, class number, torsion order and discriminant — is fully proved in Mathlib, sorry-free. That is the only proportionality statement available; Borel's theorem for j≥2 is absent.

duplicates.note: AL.1 owns the Tate zeta integrals, local functional equation, gamma factors and the global continuation/functional equation by Poisson summation that R.5's first paragraph imports.
B.2 proves that ζ_F(−1) is nonzero (and rational) for totally real F from the functional equation — the j=2, r₂=0 case of R.5's order-of-vanishing statement at 1−j.

targets.target: Local Haar/Tamagawa measures on an algebraic group over a local field and their product over all places
targets.note: Only the general existence/uniqueness of Haar measure on a locally compact group and the adele ring are available; there is no measure on an adelic group, no convergence factors, and no Tamagawa number.

targets.target: Finite-volume integrals of the adelic quotient and the discriminant/archimedean conversion factors
targets.note: No finiteness-of-volume theorem for G(F)\G(𝔸)¹ exists and `Tamagawa` has no hits. The only related results are Tau Ceti's discreteness of K in 𝔸_K (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.discreteTopology_principalSubgroup), without compactness of 𝔸_K/K, and the classical finite volume of SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ (ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top), which is not adelic.

targets.target: Primitive cohomology pairings and the comparison of Bloch's Tamagawa formulation with Borel's
targets.note: Both sides of the comparison (R.3/R.4 Borel classes and the Tamagawa description) are absent.

duplicates.note: AA.3 proves finite volume of G(F)\G(𝔸)¹ and supplies the reduction theory that the Tamagawa-measure integrals in R.6 rest on.
AA.2 constructs Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms and convergence factors, with invariant quotient measures by Weil's formula — R.6's local measures and their product.

targets.target: The Beilinson/Deligne regulator on motivic cohomology
targets.note: No Deligne cohomology (`DeligneCohomology`, `deligne cohomology` have no hits) and no motivic cohomology, so the target of the comparison does not exist.

targets.target: The precise scalar between Borel's and Beilinson's normalisations (the factor-of-2 convention) and its r-th power on determinants
targets.note: Both maps are absent, so the scalar is not statable.

targets.target: Weight-two test against the Bloch–Wigner regulator
targets.note: The Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) and Li₂(z) are not defined in either library (the only textual mention of the dilogarithm is a docstring aside in Mathlib's LogTrigonometric.lean). Mathlib does have Li_s on the unit circle: HurwitzZeta.expZeta a s continues Σ e^{2πian}/n^s, and its imaginary part sinZeta a 2 is the Clausen function, i.e. D restricted to roots of unity. No Bloch-group descent or comparison with a regulator exists.

targets.target: Zero-rank cases over ℚ and the rank-one weight-two regulator of an imaginary quadratic field
targets.note: Requires K₃ and the Bloch–Wigner map; neither exists.

targets.target: Coordinate-free maps versus computational matrices, with the linking equality
targets.note: Nothing to export.

duplicates.note: P.2 already assembles the embedding-wise Bloch–Wigner map for a number field and compares it with the Borel class including sign and scalar — the same weight-two comparison R.7 uses as its test.
M.8 constructs the real Deligne cycle-class maps and the rational regulator from motivic cohomology — the Beilinson/Deligne regulator that R.7 lists as its first target and compares with Borel's map.

EllipticKTheory.summary: The elliptic-curve half of this roadmap is far better supplied than the K-theory half. Mathlib has Weierstrass curves in affine, projective and Jacobian models with the full point group, division polynomials, normal forms and reduction; Tau Ceti adds function-field isogenies with degree, separability, kernels, invariant differentials and Frobenius, a Riemann-Roch/divisor theory for function fields, and — the sharpest hit — a sorry-free proof that E(F) is the degree-zero divisor class group (WeierstrassCurve.Affine.pointEquivDegreeZeroDivisorClass) together with the Cl ≅ Pic⁰ ⊕ ℤ degree splitting and the principality of n(T)-n(O) at an n-torsion point. What is missing is everything K-theoretic: neither library has K₀ of a scheme, K₁, K₂, K₃, a localisation sequence, tame symbols, coniveau spectral sequences, Adams operations or projective-bundle theorems, and the only K-theory present is Tau Ceti's categorical K₀ of exact/abelian/triangulated categories, which is not applied to coherent sheaves. Also absent: the elliptic curve as a Scheme (Mathlib has the general Proj construction but no curve built from it), regular proper models of arithmetic surfaces, and Tate modules. E.2's Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(F) and E.7's torsion-divisor function are genuinely already built and the roadmap treats them as work to do.

targets.target: The smooth projective scheme of a Weierstrass equation over a field, with its section at infinity
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of an ℕ-graded ring as a Scheme, and Weierstrass curves in affine, projective and Jacobian coordinates, but no elliptic curve is ever produced as an `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`: `grep -rn Scheme` over both libraries' EllipticCurve directories returns nothing. The projective model is a quotient of a point set, not a scheme.

targets.target: Affine-chart equations, smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, regularity of the curve
targets.note: Nonsingularity of a Weierstrass point is defined pointwise in Mathlib, but there is no scheme to be smooth, proper, geometrically connected or regular; Tau Ceti's AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme/Regular.lean and Morphisms/Smooth/GeometricallyReduced.lean are general and unconnected to curves.

targets.target: Identification of the function field of the scheme
targets.note: Both halves exist separately: Mathlib defines the function field of an irreducible scheme and the function field of a Weierstrass curve as the fraction field of its coordinate ring, but the two are never compared, because the scheme does not exist.

targets.target: Comparison of scheme-valued F-points and their group law with the existing Weierstrass point group
targets.note: The Weierstrass point group with its group law is fully built in Mathlib (affine, projective and Jacobian, with equivalences between them), but there is no scheme-valued functor of points to compare it with.

targets.target: Comparison of function-field isogenies with scheme morphisms; degree, separability, kernels, pullbacks of divisors, invariant differentials
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a complete function-field isogeny theory — coordinate pullbacks, degree, separability, kernel, differential, Frobenius, [n], base change — which is the 'existing function-field isogenies' side of the comparison and which the layer already treats as given. Every target of this layer nevertheless needs the scheme, which does not exist, so the comparison itself, the treatment of the zero morphism as a scheme map and the identification of divisor pullbacks under it are all absent.

duplicates.note: Layer 1A constructs the projective Weierstrass cubic as a closed subscheme of ℙ²_R with zero section and proves properness and smoothness; 1B identifies its K-points with W.toAffine.Point over a field; 1D proves the scheme group law agrees with Mathlib's pointwise one — E.1's scheme, smoothness/properness and point-group comparison over an arbitrary base ring.

targets.target: K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) for a connected regular noetherian curve (rank–determinant isomorphism)
targets.note: K₀ of a scheme (of vector bundles or coherent sheaves) is never defined, so the isomorphism has no statement for a projective curve. In the affine case both sides exist separately — Tau Ceti's K₀(proj R) as exact K₀ of finitely generated projectives over any ring, and Mathlib's Picard group CommRing.Pic (a group, ≅ ClassGroup for domains) — but no rank or determinant map K₀ → Pic, no Steinitz theorem and no K₀(R) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(R) for Dedekind domains exist. For schemes the Picard group is not a group: TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.LineBundleClass is only a commutative monoid.

targets.target: Class of a closed point, class of a line bundle, degree map, Euler characteristic, pushforward to the base
targets.note: The ingredients exist without K₀: Tau Ceti has the Euler characteristic Σ(−1)ⁱ dim Hⁱ(X, M) of a sheaf of modules on a scheme over a field, additive on short exact sequences (Scheme.Modules.eulerCharBelow), the degree of scheme Weil divisors relative to a morphism weighted by residue degrees (SchemeWeilDivisor.relativeDegree) and the function-field divisor degree; Mathlib pushes cycles forward along quasi-compact morphisms (AlgebraicCycle.map). None is a map out of a scheme's K₀, the degree of a line bundle is not defined, and no pushforward of K-classes to the base exists.

targets.target: Picard decomposition by degree on an elliptic curve with rational origin
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Cl(X) ≅ Pic⁰(X) × ℤ for an order system with a weight-one rational point, which is exactly the degree splitting of the Picard group at a rational origin, and in greater generality than the elliptic case. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(F)
targets.note: Fully proved and sorry-free: the points of a Weierstrass curve over a field with Dedekind coordinate ring are the degree-zero divisor classes of its function field, with the computation rule sending an affine point P to the class of (P)-(O). This is Silverman III.3.4, stated over an arbitrary field, and it uses the rational origin exactly as the layer requires. The roadmap does not record it.

targets.target: K₀(E) ≃ ℤ ⊕ ℤ ⊕ E(F) as a group, with tensor-product multiplication
targets.note: Depends on the first target; K₀ of the curve is undefined. Tau Ceti's SplitK0 ring structure (TauCeti.SplitK0.instCommRing) shows the tensor-product multiplication pattern at the categorical level only.

duplicates.note: Z.5 proves the rank–determinant isomorphism K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) for a connected regular noetherian curve, the structure-sheaf and skyscraper class formulas, and combines E's Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) with rank to state K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F) — E.2's first, second and last targets.

Layer 0 of the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves roadmap owns the identification of the point group with the degree-zero divisor class group and the principal-divisor characterisation (AEC III.3.4–5) — E.2's Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(F), which Tau Ceti has built.

Layer A defines Pic X, the degree of a line bundle and Pic⁰ X = ker deg on a curve — E.2's degree map and the degree decomposition of Pic, whose abstract splitting Tau Ceti's classGroupAddEquivPicZeroProdInt proves for this layer.

targets.target: The localisation sequence for a curve in degrees 0–3, over all closed points
targets.note: No K-theory localisation sequence of any kind; `localisationSequence`, `LocalizationSequence` have no hits, and K₁, K₂, K₃ are undefined.

targets.target: The tame symbol ∂ : K₂(F(X)) → ⊕_x k(x)× with its order/sign convention
targets.note: `tameSymbol` matches nothing and there is no K₂ of a field; the closest object is Tau Ceti's function-field valuation/place API, which supplies orders but no symbols.

targets.target: div : F(X)× → ⊕_x ℤ and exactness at K₀(X) → ℤ → 0
targets.note: The divisor map of a rational function and the class group exact sequence exist in Tau Ceti's function-field divisor theory, which is the bottom row of the displayed sequence; the K-theoretic terms above it do not.

targets.target: Naturality for open immersions and finite maps, with residue-field norms and ramification multiplicities
targets.note: Ramification indices, residue degrees and norms of places exist for Dedekind domains and function fields in both libraries, but there is nothing K-theoretic for them to act on.

targets.target: Comparison theorems: K₂(k(x)) torsion over a number field, zero over a finite field
targets.note: K₂ of a field is undefined, so neither the torsion statement nor the finite-field vanishing can be stated.

duplicates.note: T.3:symbols defines the tame symbol ∂_v{f,g} = (−1)^{v(f)v(g)} (f^{v(g)}/g^{v(f)}) mod v with its order/sign convention, independence of the uniformiser and the Steinberg relation — E.3's boundary map ('T's tame symbol with the same order/sign convention').

T.3:localization-comparison identifies the tame symbol with the connecting map of the K-theory localisation sequence, proves finite support of residues, and the norm/residue formula with residue degrees and ramification — E.3's boundary identification and naturality for finite maps.

S.3 constructs the localisation fibre sequence K_Z(X) → K(X) → K(U), applies it to a regular curve and identifies the boundaries on units and symbols with valuations and tame symbols — E.3's localisation sequence for a curve.

targets.target: Image of K₁(X) in F(X)× equal to F× for a proper geometrically connected curve with H⁰(X,O_X)=F
targets.note: K₁ of a scheme is undefined; H⁰(X,O_X) as a coherent-cohomology statement also has no elliptic instance (Tau Ceti has general sheaf cohomology in AlgebraicGeometry/Cohomology but no curve computation).

targets.target: SK₁ of a curve as the kernel of that map, identified with the cokernel of the tame-symbol map; constant-unit splitting
targets.note: `SK1` matches nothing in either library, in either the curve or the stable-matrix sense.

targets.target: Two-column coniveau spectral sequence of a curve and its filtration
targets.note: `coniveau` has no hits; Mathlib has spectral sequences of filtered complexes in general homological algebra but no coniveau tower.

targets.target: Adams operations and rational motivic comparison; weight eigenspaces with finite coefficients and base change
targets.note: No Adams operations (`adams` has no hits) and no motivic cohomology.

duplicates.note: M.6a owns the coniveau/support filtration and the homotopy-coniveau tower; E.4 restates the two-column case for a curve.

S.6 constructs λ-operations and Adams operations ψ^k on scheme K-theory, the eigenvalue ψ^k = k^j on weight-j rational K-theory and rational projectors — E.4's Adams operations and weight eigenspaces.

S.4 constructs the codimension filtration and coniveau exact couple of scheme K-theory, identifies its first page with residue-field K-groups and proves Gersten results — E.4's coniveau spectral sequence in general.

targets.target: K-theory pullback for arbitrary morphisms and pushforward for proper perfect morphisms; comparison with transfer for finite flat maps
targets.note: Tau Ceti has functoriality of categorical K₀ for conflation-exact functors, which would be the mechanism, but no scheme-level pullback or pushforward exists because K₀ of a scheme is undefined.

targets.target: Projection formula f_*f^*(a) = [f_*O_X]·a and the isogeny pull–push computation
targets.note: Nothing to state; Tau Ceti's isogeny degree theory (TauCeti.Isogeny.degree) exists but there is no K-theory for it to act on.

targets.target: K-theory of P¹ via the projective-bundle theorem
targets.note: `projectiveBundle` has no hits in either library.

targets.target: K-theory of an elliptic curve over a finite field via Frobenius on the Jacobian/Tate module; K₁(E/F_q) ≅ F_q× ⊕ F_q×
targets.note: The Frobenius isogeny with its degree and separable degree exists in Tau Ceti, but there is no Tate module (`TateModule` has no hits), no Hasse bound and no K-theory of a finite-field curve.

duplicates.note: S.2 constructs derived pullback for arbitrary scheme maps, pushforward for proper perfect morphisms, and proves projection formulas and affine scalar-extension comparisons — E.5's first two targets for all schemes in scope.
S.5 proves the projective-bundle theorem with generators given by powers of the tautological bundle and compares it with the ℙ¹ calculation — E.5's third target.

targets.target: A regular proper flat model 𝒔 over O_{F,S} of E/F, with minimal-regular-model / resolution results, local charts, vertical components and intersection multiplicities
targets.note: Mathlib has integral and minimal Weierstrass models over a DVR (WeierstrassCurve.exists_isIntegral, exists_isMinimal) with reduction types, and Tau Ceti adds minimality criteria and bad primes over Dedekind domains; its stable-reduction Model framework is flat, finitely presented models over a DVR with no regularity predicate. Minimal Weierstrass models are not regular models. There are no Néron models, blow-ups of schemes, intersection multiplicities on arithmetic surfaces, or regular proper models over O_{F,S}.

targets.target: The rational integral part K₂(E)_{ℤ,ℚ} = im(K₂(𝒔)⊗ℚ → K₂(E)⊗ℚ) and its S-integral variant
targets.note: K₂ of a scheme is undefined.

targets.target: Model independence via comparison of regular models, blow-up and localisation formulas
targets.note: No blow-ups of arithmetic surfaces and no K-theoretic localisation.

targets.target: The vertical-residue description using residue fields of vertical components and codimension-two compatibility
targets.note: Requires residues on K₂ of a two-dimensional regular scheme; absent.

EllipticRegulators.summary: Almost none of this roadmap exists, because its two pillars — K₂ of a curve and Deligne cohomology — are absent from both libraries, as is the dilogarithm as a function of z (Mathlib has only Li_s on the unit circle, HurwitzZeta.expZeta). What is present and relevant: Mathlib has a full Weierstrass ℘-function theory (℘, ℘′, g₂, g₃, periodicity and ℘′² = 4℘³ − g₂℘ − g₃ over an arbitrary period lattice), differential forms and curve integrals on open subsets of ℂ, cusps of arithmetic subgroups, and the Hasse–Weil L-function of a Weierstrass curve with its local Euler factors at good, split/non-split multiplicative and additive reduction; Tau Ceti has singular homology, the algebraic invariant differential, abstract weight-one Hodge structures with polarisations and Tate twists, newforms with strong multiplicity one, the Petersson product, orders of modular forms at cusps, non-vanishing of absolutely convergent ideal-weight L-series, and a large contour-integration library. Genuinely missing: the uniformisation E(ℂ) ≅ ℂ/Λ, the Tate presentation ℂ×/q^ℤ, algebraic de Rham cohomology and the period comparison, the real Deligne complex, forms such as η(f,g) on a curve, the elliptic dilogarithm D_q and its companion J_q, Bloch's divisor formula, Hecke/Größen characters and CM theory of elliptic curves, the conductor of an elliptic curve, modular curves, modular units and Manin–Drinfeld, Rankin–Selberg, p-adic L-functions and syntomic cohomology.

targets.target: The complex manifold of a smooth projective elliptic curve
targets.note: There is no elliptic curve as a scheme (see EllipticKTheory:E.1) and no complex-manifold structure on one; `RiemannSurface` has no hits in either library.

targets.target: Complex uniformisation E(ℂ) ≅ ℂ/Λ, the Weierstrass functions and the period lattice
targets.note: Mathlib has the period lattice of an ℝ-independent pair, ℘ and ℘′ with local uniform convergence, periodicity, parity, meromorphy, pole orders, the Eisenstein coefficients G, g₂, g₃ and the relation ℘′² = 4℘³ − g₂℘ − g₃ (sorry-free). Missing: that z ↦ (℘(z), ℘′(z)) induces a group isomorphism ℂ/Λ ≅ E(ℂ), the nonvanishing of g₂³ − 27g₃² (so that a lattice defines an elliptic curve), and that every elliptic curve over ℂ comes from a lattice; Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.ofJ realises every j-invariant only algebraically, and nothing links PeriodPair.G to the Eisenstein series E_k.

targets.target: Invariant differentials, homology of the curve and the intersection pairing
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the invariant differential of a Weierstrass curve algebraically (WeierstrassCurve.Affine.invariantDifferential; its docstring notes that div ω = 0 is not proved), singular homology of pairs with its long exact sequence, and π₁ of the real 2-torus ≅ ℤ × ℤ (AddCircle.prodFundamentalGroupMulEquiv). No homology group of a torus is computed and no intersection pairing on H₁ exists.

targets.target: The multiplicative presentation ℂ×/q^ℤ, q = exp(2πiτ), Im τ > 0, and change-of-basis transformations
targets.note: The upper half-plane and the q-parameter exp(2πiτ/h) with its analytic properties exist and are used throughout the modular-forms development, but there is no Tate curve ℂ×/q^ℤ (`TateCurve` has no hits) and no identification of it with ℂ/Λ.

targets.target: All complex embeddings of a number field with conjugation action, carried through the analytic construction
targets.note: Infinite places, real/complex classification and the conjugation action on embeddings are complete in Mathlib; only the elliptic-curve payload they are supposed to carry is missing.

targets.target: Comparison of algebraic de Rham cohomology, holomorphic differentials and singular cohomology; the period matrix and its nondegeneracy
targets.note: Tau Ceti has abstract pure Hodge structures with Hodge decomposition, Weil operator, polarisation and Tate twists, including the weight-one case an elliptic curve realises, and the space of regular Weil differentials of a function field with dimension equal to the genus (finrank_weilDifferentialFiltration_zero) — the algebraic holomorphic differentials. Algebraic de Rham cohomology of a variety does not exist in either library (`deRham` matches only the perfectoid period ring B_dR), so there is no comparison isomorphism and no period matrix.

duplicates.note: C5 is the algebraic de Rham–Betti comparison ER.1 says it will coordinate with a verified supplier rather than reprove.

R12.1 constructs the complex analytic manifold of a smooth projective Weierstrass curve, proves its uniformisation by ℂ/Λ compatibly with the group law, the converse construction from a lattice, and compares the invariant differential and periods — ER.1's first three targets.

targets.target: The real Deligne complex, its hypercohomology and the degree-two weight-two exact sequence
targets.note: Deligne cohomology does not exist in either library: `DeligneCohomology` and the phrase 'Deligne cohomology' have no hits. Hypercohomology of a complex of sheaves is also not available.

targets.target: The symbol regulator r_D : K₂(E) → H²_D(E_ℝ, ℝ(2)) and the dimension of its target
targets.note: Both source and target are undefined.

targets.target: The form η(f,g) = log|f| d arg g - log|g| d arg f with its differential identity and behaviour at zeros and poles
targets.note: Mathlib has differential forms on normed spaces with the exterior derivative (extDeriv, with d ∘ d = 0 and pullback) and curve integrals of 1-forms along paths with a Poincaré lemma on convex open sets (curveIntegral), so η(f,g) can be written on an open subset of ℂ; Tau Ceti's contour library adds arguments, winding numbers, residues and the argument principle. There are no differential forms on a Riemann surface or curve, and neither the identity dη(f,g) = Im(df/f ∧ dg/g) nor the behaviour of η at zeros and poles is proved.

targets.target: The Steinberg relation via the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm
targets.note: No dilogarithm and no Steinberg relation (`steinbergRelation`, `Steinberg.*relation` have no hits in a K-theoretic sense).

targets.target: Tame-symbol triviality giving the period pairing; independence of representatives, cuts and punctured cycles; the 2π factor and orientation
targets.note: Requires the tame symbol and Deligne cohomology; neither exists.

duplicates.note: M.8 constructs real Deligne cycle-class maps and the rational regulator from motivic cohomology — the universal Deligne regulator of which ER.2's r_D on K₂(E) is the curve case.
P.5 proves that unramified classes on a curve define Deligne classes and derives 'the logarithmic differential expression used by ER' in weight two — ER.2's η(f,g) and symbol regulator.

targets.target: The elliptic Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D_q as a convergent q-orbit sum
targets.note: Neither the ordinary dilogarithm Li₂ nor the Bloch–Wigner function exists in either library; the only mention of Li₂ anywhere is a docstring aside in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Integrals/LogTrigonometric.lean.

targets.target: The regularised logarithmic companion J_q and Bloch's convention R_q = J_q + iD_q
targets.note: No hits.

targets.target: Convergence, Bernoulli-polynomial correction, invariance under z ↦ qz, inversion, conjugation and lattice-basis change
targets.note: Bernoulli polynomials and their basic identities exist in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti has ample machinery for interchanging sums and integrals, but the functions whose properties are asserted do not exist.

targets.target: Fourier/Kronecker–Eisenstein descriptions with justified interchange of sums and integrals
targets.note: `KroneckerEisenstein` has no hits; Eisenstein series exist in Mathlib only as modular forms on the upper half-plane, not as Kronecker–Eisenstein series in two variables.

targets.target: The diamond convolution (f)⋄(g) = ∑ m_i n_j [Q_j - P_i] on divisors, with its sign convention
targets.note: Divisors of functions and their formal ℤ-linear algebra exist for function fields in Tau Ceti; the convolution indexed by differences of points and the translation to the group law is not defined.

targets.target: The formula relating R_q({f,g}) to evaluation on that divisor, and independence of permitted lifts
targets.note: Requires R_q from ER.3 and the symbol {f,g} from E.7; neither exists.

targets.target: Regulator of Bloch's corrected classes S_a via the divisors of ρ and f_a; vanishing of constant-symbol corrections
targets.note: No hits for Bloch's functions or classes.

targets.target: Finite Fourier transform on C-torsion and the odd-function identities
targets.note: Mathlib has the discrete Fourier transform on ZMod n with inversion and Parseval, which is the shape of the finite Fourier transform used; it is not attached to the C-torsion of an elliptic curve.

targets.target: Transfer and the trace formula for the regulator
targets.note: No K-theoretic transfer.

targets.target: A CM elliptic curve over ℚ with multiplication by the full ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field of class number one
targets.note: Class numbers and imaginary quadratic fields are available, but complex multiplication of elliptic curves does not exist in either library: `hasCM`, `ComplexMultiplication` have no hits and the endomorphism ring of a Weierstrass curve is not constructed.

targets.target: The associated Hecke (Größen)character and Deuring's comparison with the Hasse–Weil L-function, with conductor and local Euler factors including bad primes
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Hasse–Weil L-function of a Weierstrass curve with its local polynomial at every place — good reduction 1 - aT + qT², split multiplicative 1 - T, non-split 1 + T, additive 1 — so the bad-prime Euler factors the layer insists on are already built (sorry-free). Hecke characters do not exist (`HeckeCharacter`, `Grossencharacter` have no hits), so Deuring's comparison cannot be stated; neither is the conductor of an elliptic curve defined.

targets.target: Lecture 11's conductor/torsion data C = fg, the finite character, roots of unity and the Gauss/Fourier transform
targets.note: Gauss sums and the finite Fourier transform on ZMod n, with the standard normalisation lemmas, exist in Mathlib; the elliptic data they are to be applied to does not.

targets.target: The rational K₂ class U as a finite combination of the S_a, with descent to E/ℚ
targets.note: K₂ is undefined.

targets.target: Bloch's Theorem 11.2.1: L(2, χ^Gross) = π|μ_κ| χ̂(ḡ) g / (i y² C⁴) R_q(U)
targets.note: Every ingredient (the Hecke L-series, R_q, U) is missing.

targets.target: Nonvanishing of the L-value at s = 2 by absolute convergence and the Euler product
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves that the L-series of any completely multiplicative ideal weight χ : Ideal(𝓞_K) →*₀ ℂ is nonzero wherever its ideal-indexed series converges absolutely (MultiplicativeIdealWeight.LSeries_ne_zero_of_summable_idealTerm; the weight type is the carrier its docstring designates for Hecke-character arguments), and Mathlib proves a product ∏(1 + fᵢ) with summable ‖fᵢ‖ and nonzero factors is nonzero. Once the Hecke character is realised as such a weight, non-vanishing at s = 2 follows; the Hecke L-series itself is absent.

duplicates.note: CM.4 owns CM Hecke characters and their Galois realisations, which ER.5 constructs again for Bloch’s class-number-one example.

targets.target: Restriction of the regulator to the integral part of K₂
targets.note: Both the regulator and the integral part (EllipticKTheory:E.6) are undefined.

targets.target: The elliptic Beilinson conjecture: rational structure, determinant line and the period-normalised leading term at s=0
targets.note: No statement is possible; no determinant of a K-theory lattice exists.

targets.target: Equivalence of the leading-term-at-zero and L(E,2) formulations, including conductor and gamma factors
targets.note: Deligne's archimedean gamma factors and the L-function itself exist, but the functional equation of L(E,s) (which the equivalence presupposes) is not proved for any elliptic curve, and the conductor is not defined.

targets.target: The three separated conclusions (nonzero regulator of a class; determinant relation on a subspace; rank and isomorphism on the whole integral part)
targets.note: Bookkeeping over absent objects.

targets.target: The vertical-residue statement distinguishing generic unramifiedness from arithmetic integrality
targets.note: Requires residues on K₂ of an arithmetic surface; absent.

targets.target: Modular units, their divisors at cusps and the Manin–Drinfeld relation
targets.note: No modular units, Siegel units, eta quotients, Manin–Drinfeld theorem or cuspidal divisor class group exist, and there is no modular curve as a Riemann surface or scheme. The nearest results are cusps of arithmetic subgroups with finitely many orbits (Mathlib IsCusp, CuspOrbits), orders of modular forms at cusps with a valence formula for finite-index subgroups (Tau Ceti orderAtCusp, valence_formula_finiteIndex), and the Dedekind eta function (Mathlib ModularForm.eta).

targets.target: Modular-curve K₂ classes
targets.note: `ModularCurve` has no hits in either library: modular forms are developed analytically on the upper half-plane, with no algebraic or analytic modular curve.

targets.target: The regulator integral and its Rankin–Selberg/Hecke evaluation at the stated level and character
targets.note: Tau Ceti has newforms with Hecke eigenvalues, strong multiplicity one and the Petersson inner product with its adjoint formulas; Mathlib has Eisenstein series as modular forms and the abstract unfolding identity for a quotient by a discrete subgroup (QuotientGroup.integral_eq_integral_automorphize). No Rankin–Selberg integral, unfolding against an Eisenstein series or regulator integral is proved.

targets.target: Pushforward along a modular parametrisation X₀(N) → E and nonvanishing of the resulting class
targets.note: No modular parametrisation and no modularity theorem exist in either library.

duplicates.note: L0 defines Siegel functions, proves their q-expansion, transformation and divisor properties and descends powers to units on the algebraic modular curve — ER.7's modular units and their divisors at cusps.
L1 applies the K₂ symbol machinery to pairs of Siegel units on modular curves, constructing the modular-curve K₂ classes whose regulators ER.7 evaluates.

targets.target: The syntomic regulator in the good-reduction case and its comparison with explicit symbols
targets.note: `syntomic` has no hits; there is no syntomic or rigid cohomology in either library.

targets.target: p-adic elliptic integrals of the explicit symbols (Coleman integration)
targets.note: No Coleman integration; the ColemanIntegration roadmap's subject is also unbuilt in the libraries.

targets.target: The p-adic Beilinson statement with its p-adic L-function, periods and exceptional factors
targets.note: p-adic analysis exists but there is no p-adic L-function of an elliptic curve in either library, so the statement cannot be made.

targets.target: Worked examples: P¹ normalisation, CM class U with divisor and residue certificates, non-rational torsion with transfer, arithmetic-model integrality
targets.note: Examples over absent theory.

duplicates.note: Declared prerequisite owning the syntomic regulator in the good-reduction case; ER.8 is its elliptic specialisation.

L1 defines Coleman functions and Coleman integration on curves with good reduction, with Frobenius continuation and independence of choices — the p-adic integrals of ER.8's second target, for every such curve.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory.summary: Only degree zero is present, and not all of it. Tau Ceti owns the exact-category input this roadmap uses — TauCeti.ExactStructure with conflation-exact functors and transport along equivalences — together with exact, split, abelian and triangulated K₀ and their universal properties, the exact category Proj_fg(A) for any ring (proved split), the Cartan map, a resolution theorem for projective resolving subcategories, G₀ of an Artinian ring free on the simple classes, and a ring structure on split K₀ of a monoidal category; Mathlib supplies the ingredients one level up (nerves, geometric realisation, homotopy groups, model categories, the span bicategory, the core of a category, the Karoubi envelope, Serre quotients, Morita equivalence) and the cofinality lemma that a finitely generated projective is a retract of Rⁿ. Missing even in degree zero are the resolution theorem for general resolving subcategories, general dévissage, the K₀ localisation sequence, Morita invariance of K₀, cofinality under idempotent completion and the K₀ product for rings. Everything above degree zero is absent: no Q-construction, no K_n for n ≥ 1, no plus construction or BGL(A)⁺, no Waldhausen category, S-construction or spectra, no relative or nonconnective theory, no Bass Nil terms and no higher products.

targets.target: Quillen exact structures on an additive category (the stated input TauCeti.ExactStructure C)
targets.note: The exact-category input is fully built in Tau Ceti, with conflations, admissible monomorphisms and epimorphisms, extension-closed full subcategories, transport along equivalences, projectivity relative to an exact structure, and worked instances (finitely generated modules, finitely generated projectives, modules of finite projective dimension). Sorry-free.

targets.target: The category Q(C) of admissible spans, with pullback composition and representative independence
targets.note: Mathlib has the bicategory of spans whose left and right legs lie in given morphism classes, with composition by pullback (CategoryTheory.Span.comp, SpanBicat), under base-change and composition hypotheses that the deflations and inflations of an exact category satisfy. Q(C) itself — the 1-category of isomorphism classes of spans with deflation left leg and inflation right leg, with representative independence — is not constructed, and no instance for TauCeti.ExactStructure exists.

targets.target: Essentially small models, transport of the exact structure and independence, natural in exact functors
targets.note: The transport half is built: Tau Ceti transports an exact structure along an additive equivalence (ExactStructure.transport), and exact K₀ is invariant under it and under exact equivalences (ExactK0.transportEquiv, mapEquiv), with the small-model choice fixed once in GrothendieckGroup/Presentation.lean. Independence of Q(C) and of K_n from the small model, natural in exact functors, is only present in degree zero, since the Q-construction does not exist.

targets.target: K_n(C) = π_{n+1}(|NQ(C)|, 0) with its abelian-group structure
targets.note: All three ingredients — the nerve of a category as a simplicial set, its geometric realisation, and π_n of a pointed space with its group structure — exist in Mathlib, but no K-theory space or K-group is defined from them.

targets.target: π₁ NQ(C) ≅ ExactK0 C via the universal property
targets.note: The right-hand side and the universal property the comparison is supposed to use are built and sorry-free; the left-hand side is not defined.

duplicates.note: Layer 0 of the Tau Ceti GrothendieckEulerForms roadmap owns exact structures, conflation-exact functors and transfer of an exact structure along an equivalence — K.1's first target and the transport half of its small-model target.
Layer 1 fixes the small-model presentation (Shrink of a skeleton) and proves canonical choice independence of presentations — K.1's small-model independence in degree zero.
Z.6 proves that the degree-zero definitions and maps agree with π₀K from K — for rings, the comparison π₁NQ(Proj_fg(A)) ≅ K₀ that K.1 states for every exact category.

targets.target: The exact category Proj_fg(A) of finitely generated projectives
targets.note: Built and sorry-free in Tau Ceti, with the proof that the induced exact structure is the split one; see K.2:plus.

targets.target: Functorial K(A) and the plus comparison ΩQ(Proj_fg(A)) ≃ K₀(A) × BGL(A)⁺ with its cofinality statement
targets.note: Only the algebraic shadow (split K₀ is the group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes) and the module-theoretic cofinality statement (a finitely generated projective is a retract of some Rⁿ) exist; there is no functorial K(A), plus construction or BGL(A). See K.2:plus.

targets.target: Identification of the explicit K₁, K₂ and K₃ models, and Matsumoto's presentation as a field-specific theorem
targets.note: None of K₁, K₂, K₃, the Steinberg group or the Bloch group exists in either library. See K.2:low-degree-comparisons.

duplicates.note: H.4 includes 'the cofinal stabilisation argument that will identify projective-module group completion with the stable general linear group plus construction' — the plus comparison K.2 aggregates from K.2:plus.
Z.1 develops finitely generated projectives as summands of finite free modules with complements, scalar extension and ring K₀ — K.2's Proj_fg(A) and cofinality targets.
U.6 identifies π₁BGL(A)⁺ with the explicit K₁ quotient — K.2's explicit K₁ identification.
T.1:plus identifies K₂ = H₂(E(A),ℤ) with π₂ of the K-theory space — K.2's explicit K₂ identification.
V.4 proves Suslin's exact sequence relating K₃^ind(F) to the Bloch group — K.2's explicit K₃ identification.

targets.target: Identification of the explicit K₁ model (GL(A)/E(A)) with π₁ of the K-theory space
targets.note: The general linear group of matrices exists with a substantial API, and Tau Ceti proves the unstable facts SL_n(ℤ) = E_n(ℤ) and SL_n(K) = E_n(K) for a field (generation by elementary transvections), with the type-A commutator relations. The stable elementary subgroup E(A) of a general ring, the colimit GL(A), Whitehead's lemma and K₁ are not defined, so the identification cannot be stated.

targets.target: Identification of the explicit K₂ model (Steinberg group / H₂(E(A)))
targets.note: No Steinberg group of a ring: the only `Steinberg` hits are Kostant's Steinberg elements in Tau Ceti's Lie-theory files and a Steinberg basis for quaternion algebras, both unrelated.

targets.target: Identification of the explicit K₃ model
targets.note: No K₃ and no Bloch group in either library.

targets.target: Matsumoto's presentation of K₂ of a field
targets.note: Absent; no symbol presentation of any K-group exists.

duplicates.note: U.6 identifies π₁BGL(A)⁺ with the explicit quotient GL(A)/E(A), compatibly with determinant and transfer — the explicit K₁ identification this stage lists.

T.1:plus compares K₂ with H₂(E(A),ℤ) and identifies it with π₂ of the K-theory space — the explicit K₂ identification this stage lists. (Matsumoto's theorem is K2SymbolsBrauer T.2:symbols, not T.1:plus.)
V.4 proves Suslin's exact sequence 0 → Tor~(μ,μ) → K₃^ind(F) → B(F) → 0 with the degree-three map agreeing with V.1 — the explicit K₃ model this stage identifies.

targets.target: The essentially small exact category Proj_fg(A) built from the module category with projectivity and finiteness predicates
targets.note: Built exactly as the layer describes: the full subcategory of finitely generated projectives of ModuleCat R, with the exact structure induced from the abelian one, proved to be the split structure (short exact sequences with projective quotient split) and essentially small. Sorry-free. The roadmap document does not record this.

targets.target: Scalar extension along a unital ring homomorphism preserves finitely generated projectives and their split exact sequences, without a flatness hypothesis
targets.note: Mathlib proves base change preserves projectivity (Module.Projective.tensorProduct, for an algebra over a commutative ring) and finiteness (Module.Finite.base_change), and has extension of scalars ModuleCat.extendScalars only between commutative rings. Tau Ceti shows every additive functor is conflation-exact for split exact structures (ExactStructure.isConflationExact_split), which would make such a functor exact on Proj_fg. No functor Proj_fg(A) ⥤ Proj_fg(B) along an arbitrary unital ring map is constructed, and K(A) is not constructed functorially.

targets.target: Functorial K(A)
targets.note: No higher K-theory functor exists; only K₀ functoriality (TauCeti.ExactK0.map for conflation-exact functors).

targets.target: Comparison of ΩQ(Proj_fg(A)) with the direct-sum group completion of the maximal subgroupoid; π₀ = K₀(A); zero component ≅ BGL(A)⁺; the product description K₀(A) × BGL(A)⁺
targets.note: The purely algebraic shadow — split K₀ is the group completion of the additive monoid of isomorphism classes — is proved in Tau Ceti, Mathlib has the group completion of a commutative monoid, and Mathlib has the maximal subgroupoid of a category (CategoryTheory.Core). Nothing topological exists: there is no plus construction, no BGL(A), no group completion of a symmetric monoidal groupoid, no infinite-loop space and no stable general linear group.

targets.target: Cofinality: every finitely generated projective has a complement making the sum free
targets.note: Mathlib proves that a finitely generated projective module over any semiring is a retract of some Rⁿ: there are f : Rⁿ → M surjective and g : M → Rⁿ with f ∘ g = id (Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective), so M ⊕ ker f ≅ Rⁿ, and over a ring ker f = range(id − g ∘ f) is finitely generated and projective (LinearMap.ker_eq_range_of_comp_eq_id). The K-theoretic cofinality consequence belongs to the absent plus comparison.

duplicates.note: Z.1 develops finitely generated projectives as direct summands of finite free modules with the complement and splitting maps, scalar extension and ring K₀ from the split/exact universal property — K.2:plus's Proj_fg(A), scalar-extension and cofinality targets.

H.4 owns group completion of a symmetric monoidal groupoid and explicitly "the cofinal stabilisation argument that will identify projective-module group completion with the stable general linear group plus construction" — the same comparison and the same cofinality statement K.2:plus lists.

targets.target: Additivity for the exact category of conflations, and additivity of exact functors in a short exact sequence
targets.note: Only the degree-zero statement (an invariant additive on conflations descends to K₀) exists; there is no K-theory space for the additivity theorem to be about.

targets.target: Dévissage for a full abelian subcategory closed under subobjects and quotients with finite filtrations
targets.note: Only a degree-zero special case: for an Artinian ring R, Tau Ceti proves G₀(mod R) is free on the classes of the simple modules, with coordinates the Jordan–Hölder multiplicities (TauCeti.simpleClassBasis, jordanHolderCoordinate) — dévissage from finitely generated modules to semisimple ones in degree zero. Dévissage for a general abelian subcategory closed under subobjects and quotients, and in any positive degree, is absent.

targets.target: The resolution theorem for a full exact resolving subcategory, with the alternating-resolution inverse in degree zero and the comparison with the existing K₀ resolution theorem
targets.note: Only degree zero, and only the projective case. TauCeti.ExactStructure.resolutionEquiv assumes every resolving object is E-projective (hypothesis P ≤ E.isProjective), and its file states that the resolution theorem for a general resolving subcategory is not carried out. Within that case the alternating-resolution inverse (eulerClassOf, eulerHom) and the module instance K₀(proj R) ≅ K₀ of modules with finite projective resolutions (moduleResolutionEquiv) are proved. The resolution theorem for a general full exact resolving subcategory, in degree zero or on K_n, is absent.

targets.target: Quillen localisation for a Serre subcategory of a small abelian category and its quotient

HabiroNumberFields.summary: None of the four layers is built, and the reason is uniform: the roadmap sits on top of K₃, Bloch groups and p-adic regulators, none of which exist in either library, and on Habiro rings, which have no trace anywhere (`Habiro` matches nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti). What does exist, and is substantial, is the surrounding arithmetic: Mathlib has the modular and p-adic cyclotomic characters, cyclotomic extensions, the basic cyclotomic units (ζʲ − 1)/(ζ − 1) as units, power series with evaluation at topologically nilpotent elements, adic completions of Dedekind domains and completions of number fields at finite places, the Selmer group K(S, n), and arithmetic Frobenius elements; Tau Ceti has the Kummer map Kˣ → H¹(G_K, μₙ) with its kernel computed (so Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ injects into H¹), the exact sequence 1 → O_S×/n → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1, continuous Galois cohomology with low-degree long exact sequences, and cyclotomic fields with their automorphism groups and fixed fields. The genuinely missing mathematics is the whole of it: the Bloch group in either the Suslin or the CGZ convention, finite-coefficient K₃ and its Chern class, the Bockstein sequence, the group of cyclotomic units and its eigenspaces, the cyclic quantum dilogarithm and its five-term identity, the Bott element and Soulé's product formula, the Habiro ring itself (even for F = ℚ), and the K₃-indexed modules.

targets.target: The Bloch group in the CGZ and Suslin conventions, with the comparison map and its bounded 2-/6-primary difference
targets.note: `BlochGroup`, `blochGroup` match nothing, and no pre-Bloch group or five-term relation exists in either library.

targets.target: Finite-coefficient K₃ and its Chern class via the Bockstein sequence, Tate twists and Galois cohomology
targets.note: Continuous Galois cohomology of a profinite group with its long exact sequence is built in Tau Ceti on top of Mathlib's ContinuousCohomology, and the Kummer short exact sequence of discrete G_K-modules is available. K₃ with finite coefficients, the Bockstein and the Chern class do not exist; `Bockstein` has no hits in either library.

targets.target: The finite set of excluded primes for a number field F and the CGZ injectivity/isomorphism results under hypotheses on n, roots of unity, the discriminant and K₂(O_F)
targets.note: The discriminant of a number field and roots of unity are fully available, but K₂(O_F) is undefined, so the hypotheses cannot be stated and the conclusion has no content.

targets.target: The χ⁻¹-eigenspace in cyclotomic units, with a fixed cyclotomic-character convention
targets.note: The convention-fixing half of this target is already in Mathlib: the mod-n cyclotomic character (L ≃+* L) →* (ZMod n)ˣ with its uniqueness characterisation, the p-adic character valued in ℤ_pˣ with its continuity, and its compatibility with `autToPow`. Mathlib's CyclotomicUnits.lean proves the basic cyclotomic units are units — (ζʲ − 1)/(ζ − 1) for j prime to n (IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_isUnit) — and the associatedness of the ζʲ − 1, but no subgroup of cyclotomic units, χ-eigenspace or eigenspace projector on unit groups is defined.

targets.target: The norm-residue/Chern comparison and the finite-coefficient exact sequence used in CGZ §3
targets.note: The norm-residue isomorphism (Bloch–Kato/Milnor conjecture) is absent from both libraries, as is any Chern class from K-theory to étale cohomology.

H.6 constructs finite coefficients E/m for a spectrum and proves the Bockstein exact sequence 0 → πₙ(E)/m → πₙ(E/m) → πₙ₋₁(E)[m] → 0, which is the Bockstein input HB.1 uses to build finite-coefficient K₃.
M.5 proves the norm-residue isomorphism K^M_j(F)/ℓ^r ≅ H^j(F, μ_{ℓ^r}^{⊗j}) — the norm-residue theorem HB.1 says must be formalised rather than assumed.

targets.target: The cyclic quantum dilogarithm in a Kummer extension, and its change under a choice of n-th root
targets.note: No quantum or cyclic dilogarithm and no finite q-Pochhammer symbol (a;q)_n exist (Mathlib's Pochhammer file lists q-Pochhammer symbols as a TODO). The only q-product is Mathlib's Euler function ∏(1 − x^{n+1}) = (x;x)_∞ (eulerFunction) with the pentagonal number theorem, which is not the cyclic dilogarithm.

targets.target: The resulting class in units modulo n-th powers, and the distinction between units, S-units, Kummer classes and their quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the Kummer map Kˣ → H¹(G_K, μₙ), computes it on cocycles and proves its kernel is (Kˣ)ⁿ, so Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ injects into H¹; surjectivity (profinite Hilbert 90) is explicitly noted as missing in that file, so the Kummer isomorphism is not available. The S-unit bookkeeping is present: Mathlib defines the Selmer group K(S, n) of classes unramified outside S, and Tau Ceti proves the exact sequence 1 → O_S×/n → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1 (fromSUnitLift_injective, ker_toClassGroup, range_toClassGroup). Units, S-units and their ranks are in Mathlib. The cyclic-dilogarithm class itself is absent.

targets.target: The five-term identity, distribution relation, Galois action and well-definedness on the Bloch quotient
targets.note: No five-term relation of any dilogarithm exists and there is no Bloch quotient to descend to.

targets.target: CGZ Theorem 1.6 comparison with the finite Chern class, and Hutchinson's refinement R_ζ = c_ζ² for odd N
targets.note: Both sides are absent.

targets.target: Cyclic bar cycles, the Bott element and Soulé's Chern-product formula
targets.note: No Bott element (there is no K-theory spectrum), no cyclic bar construction in a K-theoretic sense, and no Soulé product formula.

targets.target: R = O_F[1/Δ] with Δ divisible by the discriminant, its compatible root-of-unity coefficient rings and their p-adic completions

review.notes: All 153 distinct citations were checked mechanically against declarations.tsv (name, file, line), for `private`, `@[deprecated]` and `sorry`, and every present-labelled target was read in the source with its hypotheses; one citation was private (removed). Every absent or partial claim in all 37 layers was re-searched by concept and by Mathlib/Tau Ceti naming in both whole trees, and each new hit was opened and verified before use. Target labels: 10 changed. Found in the libraries but called absent or understated: SL₂(ℤ) = ⟨S,T⟩, Schreier's lemma and SL_n(ℤ) transvection generation; the SL₂(ℤ) fundamental domain with finite volume; Mathlib's span bicategory with pullback composition; the cofinality lemma that a f.g. projective is a retract of Rⁿ (now mathlib); Tau Ceti's degree-zero dévissage for Artinian rings. Overclaims corrected: the K₀ resolution theorem is projective-only (P ≤ E.isProjective) and the K₀ tensor-product comparison has no higher product to compare with, so K.3 and K.7 drop to not built; K.1 small-model independence is degree zero only. Notes corrected where they denied existing material: Mathlib CyclotomicUnits.lean, the Euler function (x;x)_∞, Selmer groups K(S,n) with Tau Ceti's S-unit exact sequence, PowerSeries.eval₂ (not PowerSeries.subst) for non-formal substitution, differential forms and curve integrals, HurwitzZeta.expZeta, the Néron–Tate regulator, CommRing.Pic, sheaf-cohomology Euler characteristics, minimal Weierstrass models, cusp orders and ideal-weight L-series non-vanishing. Duplicates were the weakest part: of 98, 65 were removed (same-roadmap parents/children, KU-* checkpoints, pure suppliers or consumers, and overlaps absent from the named layer such as PS.4's Tamagawa factors or B.7), 5 re-homed to the substage that states the target (e.g. T.3:symbols for the tame symbol, S.6 for Adams operations, M.8 for the Deligne regulator), 11 notes rewritten, and 33 missed owners added (e.g. ModularCurvesPartII:R12.1 for uniformisation, AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.2 for Tamagawa measures, SchemeKTheoryOperations S.2–S.5, KatoEulerSystems L0–L1, the Tau Ceti GrothendieckEulerForms, EllipticCurves, ModularCurves and StableReduction layers). Layer order fixed to follow the batch file. E.8 stays process, consistent with the accepted acceptance-test layers HC.6, HR.7, HQ.7 and WC.7. Four roadmap summaries were rewritten to match the corrected targets.
